brief: A spending tracker where categories are geological layers — deeper is necessity, surface is discretionary

dominant_strengths: Geological metaphor is executed literally with vertical earth-strata sidebar going from light topsoil to dark bedrock — memorable and on-brief.
Warm tan/clay palette ties together the metaphor, sidebar, and right rail without feeling like a generic finance dashboard.
Reflective layer is strong: 'Depth Analysis', 'Pressure Points', stress/stability terms turn budgeting into a geological narrative.
dominant_weaknesses: The strata sidebar lacks proportional encoding — bar heights are uniform while amounts vary wildly ($320 to $2,100), wasting the metaphor's biggest affordance.
Light text on the topmost lighter strata (Surface Layer) has poor contrast, and small subtitle type across rows feels fragile.
Center panel is a generic white card list; it doesn't visually inherit the 'surface layer' identity it claims to represent.
fix_priorities: Map stratum height (or saturation) to spend amount so the geology actually visualizes the data.
Tint the active panel with the corresponding layer color so selecting a stratum feels physically continuous.
Strengthen contrast on light strata labels and unify subtitle sizes for readability.
Add subtle motion: scroll/drill-down between strata, or sediment-settle animation when adding an expense.
rationale.norman_balance: Strong reflective concept and pleasing visceral palette, but behavioral payoff is weak because the metaphor doesn't drive interaction or data encoding.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it clearly frames discretionary-to-necessity as surface-to-bedrock, though the metaphor stays decorative rather than structurally informing the spending data.
